quotedTweet.text:
We've decided to sunset Arc on December 22, 2026.

That's not an easy sentence to write. We spent years building Arc and celebrating each and every release along the way: we have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community.

Our priority is to deliver best-in-class security for our members. Keeping a browser secure takes constant, dedicated work that is only increasing in the age of AI. Dia was built from the ground up to meet today’s security standards, so that's where our engineering and security teams will focus moving forward.

We've worked to make switching to @diabrowser as easy as possible for Arc members. Here's how:

· Your passwords, bookmarks, extensions and history come over to Dia seamlessly.
· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.
· Dia now surpasses Arc benchmarks in stability, speed, and security.
· The browser features you use in Arc are free in Dia, and the AI is optional.

Thank you for using Arc, for pushing us to make it better, and for building alongside us. The team that made Arc is the same team behind Dia, and some of our most ambitious work is just ahead. We'd love for you to be there with us when it lands.

挖出这个PHP漏洞的研究员叫 j4ck3lsyn。本来在网络安全圈，一直有个不成文的规矩叫“负责任的漏洞披露”（静默期）： 👉 发现严重漏洞 ➡️ 私下报给官方 ➡️ 官方写好补丁 ➡️ 约定一个时间全球同步发布，各大网站好第一时间更新防御。
PHP 官方团队本来早就把补丁搞定了，发布时间都精确到了几点几分。
结果倒好，这位哥根本不等补丁正式落地，在静默期倒计时还没走完的时候，直接把漏洞细节甩公网了！ 攻击者拿到就能直接顺着网线打服务器，而运维甚至连补丁都还没拿到。

🤬 面对全网声讨，他的回复堪称年度最狂

当全球技术圈都在质问他为什么这么不负责任时，他直接发推硬刚，原话极其刺耳冷血：

“给那些蠢货解释一下：我没做任何违法的事，我也没和任何项目或平台签过合同，更不在乎……在当今这个世界，所谓的‘社会契约’毫无意义。所以，都给我滚蛋吧 ^.^”
最后甚至还附带了一个嘲讽拉满的笑脸颜文字 ^.^。

从纯法律角度看，他确实钻了空子：没有哪条法律强制独立研究员必须签保密协议。 这种“静默期”纯粹是技术社区三十年来靠职业伦理和道德维持的君子协定。
可当他说出“社会契约一文不值”的时候，整个开源世界的体面彻底被踩得稀烂。

👨‍💻 惨的只有谁？只有打工人！

有条热评看哭了无数人：
“现代互联网，本质上都在靠那些挖到漏洞却不滥用、默默通知开发者的好人维持着。”
大厂有重兵把守的防火墙，但遭殃的是谁？ 是医院挂号系统、学校教务网、中小公司的小程序，还有半夜三更被电话叫醒、顶着黑眼圈在无补丁状态下手动改源码防黑客的普通打工人。

拿“自由”和“叛逆”当借口，让全网毫无防备的普通技术人替他的任性买单，这真的称不上什么黑客精神，纯粹是利己主义的狂欢。

大家怎么看这种“虽然合规但毫无道德底线”的行为？评论区聊聊👇

text:
什么，真有人把炼金术研究出来了？？

旧金山一家叫 Marathon Fusion 的核聚变创业公司，刚刚发了一条相当离谱的推文。

上个月，他们宣称成功把汞变成了真正稳定的黄金，产出速率达到 CERN 此前纪录的 10 倍。

上周，又用世界上最强大的等离子体离心机完成同位素富集，声称打破了苏联保持 40 年的纪录。

然后轻描淡写地补了一句，接下来，我们要在旧金山造一座核聚变反应堆，挑战功率密度世界纪录。

炼金术、冷战时期的苏联纪录、核聚变。

我们可能已经进入了另一种末法时代。

每天醒来都能看到一些过去几百年的人想都不敢想的事情。最可怕的是，我看到这条新闻的第一反应居然只是，哦，今天又有技术突破了。

然后才意识到，哥们儿，他们说的是把水银变成黄金啊。

以前人类几代人才能见证一次的奇迹，现在每天都在发生。我们甚至来不及弄明白上一项突破意味着什么，下一项就已经出现在信息流里了。

科技越来越像神迹，而我们已经快要失去感到震惊的能力了。

Now, we’re building a fusion reactor in San Francisco to achieve record power density.

result.text:
什么，真有人把炼金术研究出来了？？

旧金山一家叫 Marathon Fusion 的核聚变创业公司，刚刚发了一条相当离谱的推文。

上个月，他们宣称成功把汞变成了真正稳定的黄金，产出速率达到 CERN 此前纪录的 10 倍。

上周，又用世界上最强大的等离子体离心机完成同位素富集，声称打破了苏联保持 40 年的纪录。

然后轻描淡写地补了一句，接下来，我们要在旧金山造一座核聚变反应堆，挑战功率密度世界纪录。

炼金术、冷战时期的苏联纪录、核聚变。

我们可能已经进入了另一种末法时代。

每天醒来都能看到一些过去几百年的人想都不敢想的事情。最可怕的是，我看到这条新闻的第一反应居然只是，哦，今天又有技术突破了。

然后才意识到，哥们儿，他们说的是把水银变成黄金啊。

以前人类几代人才能见证一次的奇迹，现在每天都在发生。我们甚至来不及弄明白上一项突破意味着什么，下一项就已经出现在信息流里了。

科技越来越像神迹，而我们已经快要失去感到震惊的能力了。

text:
The new Ponytail 5 is a complete rewrite. Same request, "add a date picker to the frontend": without it, the agent wrote 335 lines. With it, 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝟭𝟬 𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀, using the repo's existing Input component and letting the browser supply the calendar.

In the maker's own benchmark, 39 tasks in Claude Code with Opus 5.5, the agent with Ponytail wrote 53% less code, took 41% less time and cost 26% less. It wrote less, yet 𝟵𝟴% 𝗼𝗳 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗸𝘆 𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗱 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗮 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁, against 68% without.

Before writing code, it reads the parts the change touches, then asks these in order and stops at the first one that holds:
→ Does this have to be written at all?
→ Is it already in the repo?
→ Is the standard library enough?
→ Does the browser or the OS already have it?
→ Can an installed dependency cover it?
→ Can it be one line?
→ If none of that works, write the smallest version that runs, plus one small test if it has logic

Input validation, error handling, security and accessibility never get cut.

Two commands were rebuilt too. /ponytail-review used to look only for code to delete; now it also reads the code your change touches. Rename a field and break a file you never touched, and it catches that. In the maker's tests it found every problem outside the diff, against 78% without the skill. /ponytail-audit runs the same checks across the whole repo and ranks what to fix first.

5.3 also adds a bar above the Claude Code prompt: what the task cost, its tokens, how long it ran, how much existing code it reused, and whether the tests passed (needs Claude Code 2.1.290 or later).

MIT licensed, 172K stars, 8,000+ more this week. To make your agent look for what already exists before it writes, paste these into Claude Code as two separate prompts:
/plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail
/plugin install ponytail@ponytail

In Codex, run these two:
codex plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail
codex plugin add ponytail@ponytail
Then trust its two hooks in /hooks and start a new thread.

text:
The amount of hate in this thread is wild. I loved Arc for so long.

I switched to Dia a few months ago hoping that it would be Arc but with some random AI features I wouldn’t use. I was surprised to see it was actually worse than Arc in pretty much every way. UX sucked, many features missing, and even some plugins were broken in weird ways.

I finally gave up a few weeks ago and switched to Zen. So far it feels like Arc and has a few other nice touches. Plus my plugins work again. It’ll do for now.

Really sad to see this generational fumble from what was an incredible browser. I wonder if them selling out to Atlassian was the driving force behind these decisions.

quotedTweet.text:
We've decided to sunset Arc on December 22, 2026.

That's not an easy sentence to write. We spent years building Arc and celebrating each and every release along the way: we have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community.

Our priority is to deliver best-in-class security for our members. Keeping a browser secure takes constant, dedicated work that is only increasing in the age of AI. Dia was built from the ground up to meet today’s security standards, so that's where our engineering and security teams will focus moving forward.

We've worked to make switching to @diabrowser as easy as possible for Arc members. Here's how:

· Your passwords, bookmarks, extensions and history come over to Dia seamlessly.
· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.
· Dia now surpasses Arc benchmarks in stability, speed, and security.
· The browser features you use in Arc are free in Dia, and the AI is optional.

Thank you for using Arc, for pushing us to make it better, and for building alongside us. The team that made Arc is the same team behind Dia, and some of our most ambitious work is just ahead. We'd love for you to be there with us when it lands.

text:
我有个朋友，第二天要做全麻手术，前一天晚上居然打了个通宵。

医生提前告诉他，排的是第二天第一台，大概早上八九点开始。

他听完，自己琢磨出一套道理：“反正明天上手术台也得‘睡’，今晚干脆不睡了，省得浪费时间。”

然后就真开了电脑，一局接一局，愣是玩到了天亮。

第二天按时去做手术，困意倒是没耽误他什么事。

等他再睁眼，已经下午四点多了。

他迷迷糊糊转过头，发现床边坐着个人。

是麻醉医生。

对方神情严肃，正一动不动地看着他。

朋友后来跟我说，那一刻他本来有一肚子问题想问，跟医生对上眼，忽然只想先交代昨晚干了什么。

Up to $200,000 to switch your career into AI safety.

It's a grant, not a job, so there's no contract and no equity.

BlueDot grants:

• Career Transition Grants: up to $200K to go full-time on the switch, usually starting at $20K
• Rapid Grants: up to $20K for living costs, compute, travel or events
• Fully remote
• You don't need to have taken any of their courses
• Covers AI safety and biosecurity work

Their words: "You do not need a conventional AI safety background."

What to know:
• Transition grants are full-time only, and you'll need evidence you're already making the move
• Some countries can't receive payments, so check their list first
• Unused money goes back if you land a job mid-grant
• Master's and PhD programs generally aren't funded

Rolling applications with no deadline.

Bookmark it and send it to the engineer who keeps saying they'd work on AI safety if they could afford to.

text: Bayern are not planning a particular transfer splurge following the injection of around €250m into the club's coffers from the Viessmann deal. While several important contract extensions with key players (Kane, Olise) remain on the agenda, the club is currently not planning to reinvest the money into the squad. Instead, Bayern want to use the proceeds specifically to invest in the club’s future. Infrastructure, sustainability and digitalisation will play a particularly central role. The club’s leadership sees significant potential for development in these areas and wants to ensure that Bayern are optimally positioned across as many areas as possible for the years ahead. The thinking behind that is simple: Not every million has to be spent immediately on the transfer market. Rather, Bayern want to use their financial strength to further improve the conditions surrounding the club and ensure that FC Bayern remains competitive in the long term [@Plettigoal, @SkySportNews]

text:
目前的 Harness 优化，有两个大方向。

一统全局脚手架，试图用一套Prompt 和控制逻辑。但随着业务场景增加，针对财务表格优化的指令往往会干扰代码生成任务，导致严重的规则冲突与上下文过度膨胀。

另一种是针对每个特定领域单独复制一份专用代码。然而不同版本之间无法代码复用，维护起来很难。而且一旦遇到未曾见过的分布外（OOD）新任务，专用脚本往往会崩溃，且无法回退。

其实人类软件工程早在 40 年前，就用面向对象编程完美解决了复用、特化与隔离的问题。

那么，为什么不把这套直接用在 Agent Harness 的自动演化上？

Google Cloud AI Research 联手 UIUC 团队，刚刚在 arXiv 上发表了一篇论文：Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design

他们提出了 OO-Harness，首次将面向对象设计（OOP）的继承、封装与多态引入智能体脚手架的自我演化中。

OO-Harness 的设计哲学非常纯粹，就是将 Agent Harness 直接建模为一组可执行的 Python 类层级体系。
首先定义一个标准的基础类，封装最通用的核心执行逻辑、基础工具接口与容错底座，确保系统在任何时候都有稳固的下限。
演化 Agent 采用 Claude Opus 4.8 深度剖析历史失败日志，自动捕捉特定业务集群的痛点，并自主编写新的 Python 子类。

子类直接继承 Base 的通用控制力，仅针对性地重写特定方法。

测试阶段是由路由 Agent 结合初始执行证据比如第一轮报错日志或环境状态，精准定夺。

如果匹配到已知痛点，立即指派给特化子类 Harness 执行。如果发现是陌生的分布外任务，系统安全降级调用 Base Harness，彻底杜绝了盲目特化导致的误伤。

这项研究中他们把底层的执行大模型gemini-3.5-flash完全冻结，不调一个参数，仅仅依靠演化这套 OOP 代码 harness，在三大长程复杂基准上刷出性能跨越
覆盖金融、HR、营销、销售等长链条业务，主指标综合得分从 61.62% 至 77.41%。严苛任务通过率从 25.44% 至 37.22%，同时由于逻辑更加精简直接，平均执行步数反而减少了 3.28 步。
此外在极其繁杂的文档、幻灯片与表格跨应用任务中，综合得分从 25.45% 至 39.48%。
多工具复杂交互中得分稳步从 71.87% 推进至 77.18%。
在面对未曾见过的分布外任务时，传统的自演化方法因为把过度拟合的专用规则强行套用在新任务上，通过率直接跌至 44.90%；

而 OO-Harness 凭借面向对象的安全兜底机制，自动识破陌生场景并复用 Base 基类，保持了59.18% 的表现。
OO-Harness 给整个 AI 工程指明了一条无比清晰且优雅的道路。
把 Agent 当一段具备状态的软件工程实体。

把面向对象的继承与封装，当做 AI 自动演化、自我重构的载体，能很好的解决代码复用和泛化退步的问题。

推荐所有在 Agent 生产环境落地、工具链治理与长程复杂工作流架构的读这篇

text:
Everyone with a camera and claude should have a world class tennis coach.  

@brainsandtennis and I chained open-source models post-trained on tennis to track players, ball, court, and labeled every stroke with its type and a 65-joint skeleton.

We then post-processed this data into 30+ biomechanical traits across serves, forehands and backhands, normalized for each player’s build and the camera.  

Turns out Claude is a wonderful coach :)

quotedTweet.text:
Why hasn’t AI already revolutionized sports analytics?

We turned 34 hours of tennis videos of 11 ATP pros into precise measurements of how each player hits.

We then measured @BrainsAndTennis and @phamrich_. Turns out Claude is an exceptional tennis coach.

https://t.co/vrf7qxMeI3

We've decided to sunset Arc on December 22, 2026.

That's not an easy sentence to write. We spent years building Arc and celebrating each and every release along the way: we have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community.

Our priority is to deliver best-in-class security for our members. Keeping a browser secure takes constant, dedicated work that is only increasing in the age of AI. Dia was built from the ground up to meet today’s security standards, so that's where our engineering and security teams will focus moving forward.

We've worked to make switching to @diabrowser as easy as possible for Arc members. Here's how:

· Your passwords, bookmarks, extensions and history come over to Dia seamlessly.
· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.
· Dia now surpasses Arc benchmarks in stability, speed, and security.
· The browser features you use in Arc are free in Dia, and the AI is optional.

Thank you for using Arc, for pushing us to make it better, and for building alongside us. The team that made Arc is the same team behind Dia, and some of our most ambitious work is just ahead. We'd love for you to be there with us when it lands.

text:
一个漂亮女生，和男朋友谈了4年，双方家长都开始催婚了

但一个从未见过的陌生男人，只用一通6小时的电话，就让她买机票飞去成都
当天，两人发生了亲密关系，据说还是内S
但她的男朋友，什么都不知道。

她自己也亲口说过：

“我男朋友对我非常好，我也非常爱他。”

可没人能想到，她仅仅因为给一个陌生男人的小狗视频点了个赞，几天后，竟然瞒着男友飞去成都，和那个男人发生了亲密关系

而在此之前，两人甚至从未见过面。

他们之间最关键的一次交流，是一通361分钟的电话。

将近6个小时。

四年的感情，没能挡住这短短几天的诱惑

这是2026年9月，一名中国博主在YouTube视频中讲述的亲身经历

按照他的说法，9月4日，他注意到一个漂亮女生给自己的小狗视频点了赞。

于是主动发了一句：

“Hi。”

女生回复了。

一开始，两个人并没有聊得多热络

女生经常只回几个字，偶尔发个表情包。

但后面不算的交流下，两人的关系突然升温

他们打了一通长达361分钟的电话。

电话打到一半时，女生告诉他：

自己已经有男朋友了。

两人交往了四年，男朋友对她非常好，她也很爱男朋友，男朋友据说也非常帅，比这位博主更帅

男人听完沉默了一会，问了一个问题：

“如果我比你男朋友先认识你，你会喜欢谁？”

女生回答：

“你。”

男人又问她，愿不愿意跟自己谈恋爱。

她说愿意。

但紧接着又补了一句：

“我肯定不能两个谈两个，对你对谁都不公平。”

但接下来，她开始认真研究：

怎样才能瞒着男朋友，去见这个刚认识的男人？她说非常想见他，即使不谈恋爱，想做什么大概成年人都懂吧

男人住在成都

她人在上海偶尔去深圳

为了不让男朋友发现，她提出了好几个方案，称为ABC方案

让闺蜜陪自己飞成都，再让闺蜜返回。

或者谎称去深圳找朋友，实际转机去成都

甚至连该找哪个朋友帮忙，谁不会向男友告密，她都考虑过

这时候两个人还没有见过面。

男人原本以为，她可能只是说说而已。

没想到第二天，女生突然发来一条消息：

“来接我。”

她真的买了机票。

独自飞到了成都

一个已经交往四年，家里正在催婚的女生，就这样瞒着男朋友，去见了一个几天前还完全不认识的男人。

两人见面当天，就发生了亲密关系。

而她的男朋友，对这一切毫不知情。

当天晚上，两人在酒吧聊天。

男人突然问她：

“假如你怀了我的孩子，你男朋友会认吗？”

女生回答：

“他肯定不知道有你的存在啊。”

“那我怀孕了，肯定是他的问题啊。”

男人接着问：

“除非去做亲子鉴定？”

“他会做吗？”

“他不会。”

这段对话，博主播放了录音

而他在视频中也承认，自己参与这件事的做法很不妥，并对此感到后悔

text:
旧金山聚变公司 Marathon Fusion 称用中子把水银变成了金子，金价不会受影响，他们真正要卖的是抗癌药原料

Marathon Fusion 是旧金山一家 28 人的创业公司。10 月 21 日，公司在 X 上发帖说，上个月他们用核聚变产生的中子，把水银（汞）变成了稳定的金子，速度是欧洲核子研究中心 CERN 2025 年纪录的 10 倍。

先回答最实际的问题：金价会跌吗？不会。

按 Marathon 自己 2025 年论文的算法，一座吉瓦级的聚变电站外面包一层水银，每年能顺带产约 2 吨金子。2025 年全球金矿产量约 3672 吨，要追上这个数，得建 1800 座这样的电站，而眼下一座都没有。Marathon 自己的装置功率是 1 千瓦，只有吉瓦的百万分之一。

这样产出的金子还混着放射性，联合创始人 Adam Rutkowski 去年对英国《金融时报》说，要存放 14 到 18 年才完全安全。

这次实验本身的量也小。CERN 那项纪录是对撞机里铅原子核擦肩而过、被打掉 3 个质子变成的金，2015 到 2018 年四年一共约 29 皮克，不到一克的三百亿分之一，最快时每秒约 8.9 万个原子。

Marathon 说的是“高速率”，比的应该是每秒产量，但公司没说比的是哪个数，也没公布一共做出多少金子、纯度多高。外媒指出，帖子里的证据只有一张伽马射线能谱图，目前没有第三方验证。

原理物理学家早就知道。氘和氚两种氢聚变时，每次反应都会甩出一个速度极快的中子。这个中子撞进汞-198，会顺带再撞出一个中子，剩下的汞-197 过几天自己衰变成金-197，也就是首饰里那种金。普通核电站里这么快的中子很少，聚变装置每反应一次就有一个。

那一家聚变公司为什么要炼金？答案在钱上。

Marathon 今年 2 月发了一篇论文，给每一个聚变中子算了价钱：拿去发电，按每度电约 0.1 美元算，一个中子值约 3×10⁻²⁰ 美元；拿去炼金，值 2.6×10⁻²⁰ 美元，跟发电差不多；拿去做钼-99，值 2.6×10⁻¹⁷ 美元，接近发电的一千倍；拿去做抗癌药原料锕-225，值约 10⁻¹⁰ 美元，是发电的 30 亿倍左右。

这个账决定了聚变装置多早能赚钱。论文算出，只卖电的聚变电站，等离子体放出的能量要达到加热它所用能量的 10 到 22 倍才能回本，现有实验装置离这个门槛还很远。如果同时卖电和金子，门槛降到 3 倍左右。如果专做钼-99，放出的能量只有投入的千分之一也能赚钱。

钼-99 衰变出的锝-99m 是核医学检查里用得最多的显像剂，约八成的核医学扫描靠它，现在主要靠全球少数几座研究用反应堆裂变铀来生产。Marathon 去年 12 月的论文估计，一台 3 兆瓦、远达不到能量回本的聚变装置，就能满足全世界的钼-99 需求。

锕-225 更稀缺。它用于靶向放射治疗：把放射性原子挂在能认出癌细胞的药物分子上，送到肿瘤旁边近距离照射。这类药的市场在长，诺华的前列腺癌药 Pluvicto 2025 年卖了约 20 亿美元。锕-225 长期主要靠美国橡树岭国家实验室从冷战时期留下的核材料里慢慢提取。Marathon 官网写的路线是用聚变中子轰击镭-226 来生产它。

这次帖子里，公司说已经做出第一批医用同位素：用聚变中子轰击锌，得到铜-64 和铜-67。铜-64 用于 PET 扫描找肿瘤，铜-67 用于治疗。产量没有公布。

所以 Marathon 的计划分两步：先用小装置卖医用同位素，以后再靠金子给大型聚变电站补贴收入。论文估计全球黄金市场每年约 7000 亿美元，足够支撑约 2 太瓦（2000 吉瓦）的聚变发电。这些都是公司自己的模型，还没有一笔真实销售。

为了产够中子，Marathon 说要每秒把一万亿个中子打进一个 1 厘米大小的靶子，连续好几年。他们正在旧金山建的装置用加速器把氘离子打到含氚的锂靶上，用途是产中子，不发电。公司的目标是从现在起每月把功率密度翻一倍，这是计划，还没有实际记录。

帖子里还提到，上周他们在“全球最强的等离子体离心机”里富集了同位素，打破了苏联保持 40 年的纪录。这种离心机让带电的气体高速旋转，重的同位素甩到外圈，轻的留在中间。汞-198 只占天然汞的一成左右，炼金前得先这样挑出来。公司没说打破的是哪项纪录、数值是多少。

旧金山聚变公司 Marathon Fusion 称用中子把水银变成了金子，金价不会受影响，他们真正要卖的是抗癌药原料

Marathon Fusion 是旧金山一家 28 人的创业公司。10 月 21 日，公司在 X 上发帖说，上个月他们用核聚变产生的中子，把水银（汞）变成了稳定的金子，速度是欧洲核子研究中心 CERN 2025 年纪录的 10 倍。

先回答最实际的问题：金价会跌吗？不会。

按 Marathon 自己 2025 年论文的算法，一座吉瓦级的聚变电站外面包一层水银，每年能顺带产约 2 吨金子。2025 年全球金矿产量约 3672 吨，要追上这个数，得建 1800 座这样的电站，而眼下一座都没有。Marathon 自己的装置功率是 1 千瓦，只有吉瓦的百万分之一。

这样产出的金子还混着放射性，联合创始人 Adam Rutkowski 去年对英国《金融时报》说，要存放 14 到 18 年才完全安全。

这次实验本身的量也小。CERN 那项纪录是对撞机里铅原子核擦肩而过、被打掉 3 个质子变成的金，2015 到 2018 年四年一共约 29 皮克，不到一克的三百亿分之一，最快时每秒约 8.9 万个原子。

Marathon 说的是“高速率”，比的应该是每秒产量，但公司没说比的是哪个数，也没公布一共做出多少金子、纯度多高。外媒指出，帖子里的证据只有一张伽马射线能谱图，目前没有第三方验证。

原理物理学家早就知道。氘和氚两种氢聚变时，每次反应都会甩出一个速度极快的中子。这个中子撞进汞-198，会顺带再撞出一个中子，剩下的汞-197 过几天自己衰变成金-197，也就是首饰里那种金。普通核电站里这么快的中子很少，聚变装置每反应一次就有一个。

那一家聚变公司为什么要炼金？答案在钱上。

Marathon 今年 2 月发了一篇论文，给每一个聚变中子算了价钱：拿去发电，按每度电约 0.1 美元算，一个中子值约 3×10⁻²⁰ 美元；拿去炼金，值 2.6×10⁻²⁰ 美元，跟发电差不多；拿去做钼-99，值 2.6×10⁻¹⁷ 美元，接近发电的一千倍；拿去做抗癌药原料锕-225，值约 10⁻¹⁰ 美元，是发电的 30 亿倍左右。

这个账决定了聚变装置多早能赚钱。论文算出，只卖电的聚变电站，等离子体放出的能量要达到加热它所用能量的 10 到 22 倍才能回本，现有实验装置离这个门槛还很远。如果同时卖电和金子，门槛降到 3 倍左右。如果专做钼-99，放出的能量只有投入的千分之一也能赚钱。

钼-99 衰变出的锝-99m 是核医学检查里用得最多的显像剂，约八成的核医学扫描靠它，现在主要靠全球少数几座研究用反应堆裂变铀来生产。Marathon 去年 12 月的论文估计，一台 3 兆瓦、远达不到能量回本的聚变装置，就能满足全世界的钼-99 需求。

锕-225 更稀缺。它用于靶向放射治疗：把放射性原子挂在能认出癌细胞的药物分子上，送到肿瘤旁边近距离照射。这类药的市场在长，诺华的前列腺癌药 Pluvicto 2025 年卖了约 20 亿美元。锕-225 长期主要靠美国橡树岭国家实验室从冷战时期留下的核材料里慢慢提取。Marathon 官网写的路线是用聚变中子轰击镭-226 来生产它。

这次帖子里，公司说已经做出第一批医用同位素：用聚变中子轰击锌，得到铜-64 和铜-67。铜-64 用于 PET 扫描找肿瘤，铜-67 用于治疗。产量没有公布。

所以 Marathon 的计划分两步：先用小装置卖医用同位素，以后再靠金子给大型聚变电站补贴收入。论文估计全球黄金市场每年约 7000 亿美元，足够支撑约 2 太瓦（2000 吉瓦）的聚变发电。这些都是公司自己的模型，还没有一笔真实销售。

为了产够中子，Marathon 说要每秒把一万亿个中子打进一个 1 厘米大小的靶子，连续好几年。他们正在旧金山建的装置用加速器把氘离子打到含氚的锂靶上，用途是产中子，不发电。公司的目标是从现在起每月把功率密度翻一倍，这是计划，还没有实际记录。

帖子里还提到，上周他们在“全球最强的等离子体离心机”里富集了同位素，打破了苏联保持 40 年的纪录。这种离心机让带电的气体高速旋转，重的同位素甩到外圈，轻的留在中间。汞-198 只占天然汞的一成左右，炼金前得先这样挑出来。公司没说打破的是哪项纪录、数值是多少。

text:
Michael Olise was a 58.
One season later: 99.

Declan Rice: 55 → 89.
Khvicha Kvaratskhelia: 61 → 89.

None of them looked like a star on paper. All of them were sitting in the same place: the 50–70 band, where most people stop looking.

So we went back and read every U23 season since 2016.

→ 1,327 seasons started in the 50–70 band
→ 12% of them hit 80+ the very next year
→ up to a third of next season's 80+ players come from that band

The ones who jumped had six things in common:

1. They played a lot
2. Clean passing
3. Busy without the ball
4. They beat their man
5. They got into the box
6. They scored less than their shots deserved, and that kind of luck comes back

We put this season's 1,700 candidates through the same test. The top three:

🟢 Santiago Castañeda (21, DM, Paderborn): 7.0× the average candidate's chance
🟢 Archie Gray (20, DM, Tottenham): defensive actions in the top 2%
🟢 Bil Nsongo (22, ST, Deportivo): unlucky finishing, the kind that turns

Filter by position, price or age, and every player tells you exactly why he's on the list.

A place to start watching. Not a verdict.

Breakout candidates. Now on NEXUS. 👇

每一句断语都对照倪海厦《天纪》原话和《紫微斗数全书》原文校正过，引文逐字可查。全部按规则算出来，不经 AI 生成，同一张盘每次结果都一样。

压缩后只有 161MB，按出生年份一年一个文件。CC BY 4.0，可以商用，细则见仓库 README。

搭排盘网站直接查表，训练命理大模型直接当语料。仓库已经 5,400 多颗星，欢迎拿去用。

text:
卧槽兄弟们，这个真的牛逼，感觉大模型诞生至今最憋屈的七年失忆史可能要翻篇了！！

甚至我想说个暴论，这大概是今年大模型架构演进里最性感、但也最击中行业要害的一次底层突围。

刚刚开源的 MemT-1.0 第一次在 Transformer 底层焊入了一颗真正的生物级海马体，

让 AI 从聊完即忘的失忆金鱼，真正进化成了能把经验沉淀进血液里的生命体。

靠暴力堆显卡、拿几个 G 的 KV Cache 硬撑长文本的旧石器时代，今天被这个开源原生记忆大模型正式砸穿了。

他们放出的 66 页技术报告和最高 288B 的开源权重直接甩出了一组降维打击的工程账单：

把记忆变成前向计算流的原生状态后，256K 超长历史下的显存开销从 5.06 个 G 暴降到恒定的 40 兆，
直接把 KV 缓存砍掉了整整一百二十倍以上，而且首字延迟更是不管历史拉得多长，始终稳稳压在一百毫秒出头。

最先击穿传统路径的，是它彻底重构了模型的前向计算流。

以前大家为了让 AI 记住上下文，只能硬着头皮堆长文本或者外挂向量库，代价就是显存撑爆且丢失多步推理因果，它在标准网络旁并联了一套原生记忆模块，在输入进入的瞬间，擦除门、写入门和遗忘门就像生物海马体一样自动运转，不再保留所有的死文字，而是把信息实时消化成动态的内部记忆矩阵。

更绝的是它在真实智能体场景下带来的降维打击，团队把历史纠错中沉淀的一千多条代码经验，直接写入内部的原生记忆状态，完全不占用任何系统提示词的 Token 额度，

结果在标准代码测试集上，连续三次均通过的硬核指标直接提升了百分之八，稳定性甚至反超了直接塞明文提示词的做法。

这意味着经验不再是一段需要模型每次重新阅读理解的生硬规则，而是直接内化成了它的本能直觉，真是牛逼!

我觉得这才是通往真正的递归自我改进最底层的物理逻辑啊, 参数只定义了模型的出厂下限，但唯有持久内化的原生记忆，才能为智能打开复利增长的空间。

以前我们买的模型是聊完即焚的一次性计算工具，从今天起模型正在变成越用越懂业务、越用越值钱的自进化资产。

大家在做智能体或者长对话应用时，最头疼的是长上下文带来的昂贵显存和卡顿延迟，还是模型转头就忘业务规范的失忆症？
对我来说，光是把 256K 显存压缩一百二十倍且延迟恒定这一项，就已经能让无数原本算不过账的长程业务直接原地复活了hh~

卧槽，又挖到一个减少付款摩擦的 trick：

刚改完上线，就来了一个用户，直接付了 400 多美金的年费订阅🤣

用户不用登录，点完价格直接进 Stripe 付款页。

付款时填的邮箱，就是他的账号。

webhook 收到付款，后台用这个邮箱自动注册，之后直接用邮箱登录就能用。

少了注册这一步，付款前就少了一个流失点。

有个坑要注意：

这个邮箱要是以前注册过，购买得直接记到老账号上。不然他换个浏览器登录，会发现钱付了啥也没有。

· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.
· Dia now surpasses Arc benchmarks in stability, speed, and security.
· The browser features you use in Arc are free in Dia, and the AI is optional.

Thank you for using Arc, for pushing us to make it better, and for building alongside us. The team that made Arc is the same team behind Dia, and some of our most ambitious work is just ahead. We'd love for you to be there with us when it lands.

text:
非常推荐读一下 OpenAI FDE 负责人 Colin Jarvis 今天发的这篇工程博客！

他们的 FDE 团队花了几个月给客户做 AI 系统，结果 Codex 变强后，直接删掉了约 90% 的定制代码。

文章用一个半导体客户的真实项目，讲清楚了 FDE 到底在做什么。

工程师直接深入客户团队，跟芯片专家一起设计 Eval、搭建 Harness，把 AI 真正用到芯片验证和调试流程里。

在这个行业，验证约占项目工作量的 70%。前 3–6 个月，几个场景都上了生产：定向测试生成节省约 48% 的时间，几周的调试被压缩到几小时。

但项目上线只是第一步。

随着 Codex 能力提升，团队把原来的定制应用逐步改造成通用 Harness 上的 Skills 和插件。Codex 本身成了交互界面，原来各场景单独写的终端界面和命令行工具全部退役。

扩展到新团队时，基本只需要换上新的连接器和 MCP，再用一个 Skill 生成新的 Eval。第一次部署花了两个月，复制到第二个团队只用了一天。

而当模型能力不够时，FDE 还要把真实业务中的失败案例和能力缺口反馈给 Research。一家电信客户做语音客服，模型一开始在关键 Eval 上只有约 60%，六个月里随着新模型迭代涨到 90% 以上，才达到上线标准。

我很喜欢作者提到的一个目标：让 FDE 不断减少别人对自己的依赖。

我觉得企业 Agent 项目里真正留得下来的，是 Eval、失败案例和沉淀成 Skill 的业务知识；为了补模型短板写的胶水代码，每次模型升级都该重新审一遍，随时准备删。

做企业 AI 落地的建议先收藏。如果你每接一个新客户都还在从头写一套，说明东西还停在定制应用这一层，没沉淀下来。

原文：https://t.co/IQt7Ssve87

1. Zen：Firefox 内核、开源，Space 手感最像 Arc，提名最多

3. Phi：Chromium 内核，一个开关关掉全部 AI
4. Helium：Chromium 内核，极简，默认内置 uBlock Origin
5. Crest：Mac + iPhone 原生，iCloud 同步
6. Dia：官方继任者，一键迁移，但没有 Air Traffic Control 和 Little Arc
7. Lumno：不换浏览器，给 Chrome 补回 Arc 的命令栏和自动画中画

你换哪个？

text:
i'm begging you: stop applying on job boards. cold email founders instead. the exact play, with the data:

1. find 25 startups that raised a seed round 2 to 9 months ago. fresh money means hiring. under 2 months they're still scrambling. free sources: inc42 and entrackr funding trackers, wellfound's recently funded filter.

2. keep only the ones under 30 people. below 30, the founder still reads their own inbox.

3. pull 2 contacts per startup: the founder plus whoever runs the function you want. emailing more than one contact lifts replies 93%.

4. the email: 90 to 120 words. line 1 is about their raise or their product, not you. subject 36 to 50 characters (long subjects get 32.7% more replies). personalize the body (+32.7%). no resume attached. end with one question: 'what are you struggling to hire for right now?'

5. send wednesday morning, 9 to 11, their timezone. best day in the data.

6. follow up once on day 4. a single follow-up adds 65.8% more replies. once more on day 9, then stop forever.

7. the math: 25 startups x 2 contacts = 50 emails. average cold outreach converts 8.5%, that's 4 replies even done plainly. stack the multipliers and you're at 8 to 12 replies, 3 to 4 calls, 1 to 2 offers.

50 emails and one weekend to build the list. job boards put you in a queue. this puts you in a conversation.

原博主被封号了，昨天刚研究明白。他这个商业模式有点意思。大概就是跟老婆抽粉丝拍ntr的黄片收群费。干了几十万会员。
然后去线下陪玩店，以在粉丝群引流名义，带着偷拍设备点漂亮妹妹
然后说自己是m，教妹妹打飞机。哄骗妹妹给她打飞机或者做更深入的加菜。
看了几部片子，这货打飞机确实有点东西，很多人跟他比一辈子飞机都白打了。

大致工作流
1.寸止三起三落,要射就停
2.高潮毁灭，射的前一刻停，让精液流出来(Ruined Orgasm)
3.强制高潮，步骤2之后，男的一般射不出来了，还能硬。就硬打给他打出来。也可以跳过这一步
4.龟责，射后虐龟头，折磨+臣服

跟grok探讨了一下，他这里面心理学的点。是权力交换 + 预期落差 +羞耻 臣服感+被剥夺感。。里面的角色也可以男女互换，不是很懂，分享给变态的你。

text:
How to become AI Advisor in 2026:

i run a $60-70k/mo distribution agency and do AI advising in it daily

without AI advising i'd never close the high-ticket clients

here's the full 6-stage roadmap:

STAGE 1: pick one industry before you pick any model

- spend your time learning which process bleeds money
- pick the vertical you already have context in
- learn their margins, their tools, their vocabulary
- specialists charge 20-30% over generalists for identical work

STAGE 2: automate your own operations first

- do it on your real business, end to end
- write down what broke, what you abandoned, what each run costs
- that write-up becomes your portfolio and it outsells any certificate

STAGE 3: do 3 audits for free

- 2 hours inside the business, watching how work actually moves
- time and cost every repetitive process you see
- hand back one page, cuts ranked by payback period
- that one page is the skill they pay for later

STAGE 4: turn the audit into a product with tiers

- discovery, 1-2 weeks, 3-5 stakeholder interviews and a readiness scorecard, $1.5-3k
- comprehensive, 2-4 weeks, diagnostic across data, infra, talent and governance plus a prioritized use case matrix, $5-15k
- strategy and roadmap, 4-8 weeks, implementation plan, vendor evaluation, budget, $15-50k
- tiered packages convert 35-40% better than hourly proposals

STAGE 5: ship one of your own recommendations

- keep your hands in the build, month two is when that shows
- take the smallest cut on your own map and implement it
- measure hours and dollars before and after, in writing

STAGE 6: treat the assessment as the front door to the real contract

- a $10k assessment is paid discovery for a $150k implementation
- advisory retainer after that runs $1-3k/mo, more in regulated verticals
- price on deliverables and you move past $200/hr

HOW TO LAND THE FIRST CLIENT:

- start growing your X & LinkedIn, it's literally the best selling channel you have
- publish one audit a week in your socials and let the buyers identify themselves
- join their trade groups and industry slacks, in AI rooms you only meet competitors
- offer their bookkeeper, agency and lawyer 10-20% to make the introduction
- spot a company hiring someone to do reports by hand, then message the manager
- record a 5 minute teardown of their process and send it with no pitch
- charge small for a 90 minute workshop and audit whoever stays after
- if they loved the audit, send a detailed proposal and wait for the yes

soon i'll prepare detailed long-form tweet or article on how to attract buyers into your B2B business

which tricks are working right now, which are not really efficient and better to avoid them

ai advising is not theoretical stuff... you should build, show, prove your efficiency

you should spend a lot of time for warming up the clients, since usually buyers are ready to pay highly

learn it, implement it daily and THE MAIN, show in public, share what you do and give a chance to your buyers to see potential output before sell

gl

someone who can walk into a business, look at their operations for 2 hours, and say "this process right here? AI cuts it by 40% and here's exactly how"

be that guy

text:
勇闯Perp价差套利第一周，供大家参考：

延迟：（我的服务器在 AWS 东京）

@arcus_xyz：挂单 43ms，改价 28ms，撤单 52ms，挂单成交到收到推送 10ms 左右

@Lighter_xyz ：357ms，其中 300ms 是 Standard 档固定的吃单延迟，网络往返只有 33ms

@entropyIO：540ms 撮合，780ms 收到回执

540ms 里网络只占很小一部分，东京到交易所的往返通常只有几十毫秒。剩下的大部分应该是 Hyperliquid 链上出块、撮合的等待时间

每组 2个号，本金 = 两边账户合计

A 组｜Entropy × Lighter RH 
运行 4.8 天｜本金 $205｜交易量 $12,035｜平均 OI $404
盈利 +$6.01

B 组｜Arcus × Lighter RH（保守）
运行 7 天｜本金 $282｜交易量 $20,269｜平均 OI $699
盈利 +$2.69｜积分 1.26

C 组｜Arcus × Lighter RH（均衡）
运行 4.8 天｜本金 $411｜交易量 $47,463｜平均 OI $1,361
盈利 +$4.27｜积分 1.94

D 组｜Arcus × Lighter RH（激进）
运行 2 天｜本金 $200｜交易量 $31,593｜平均 OI $819
盈利 +$1.94｜积分 0.87

Arcus × Lighter（B + C + D）合计：本金 $893，交易量 $99,325，盈利 +$8.90，Arcus积分 4.07，Lighter给的积分总共不到0.3😂😂

Arcus积分跟什么有关：

OI x 持仓时间、交易量

大约每 1 万刀交易量 0.17 分，每 1000 刀 OI 持仓一天 0.18 分，三组的误差都在 4% 以内。

也就是说，持仓 1000 刀 OI 一整天，差不多相当于刷 1 万刀交易量。

各品种表现：（我只选择了流动性还不错的RWA品种，Crypto只做了ZEC）

CRCL 赚得最多，SPCX 滑点最大、SPY滑点最小，只有ZEC是亏得。

text:
Arc is the reason I will never switch browsers ever again.

I used Chrome for years and years and years but, despite the high switching costs, Arc was cool enough for me to pull the trigger and try something new. 

I loved, I recommended it to friends. It was buggy but I really really loved it. Just yesterday I was using Chrome with vertical tabs and reminiscing on how good Arc’s tab management was, how much I enjoyed using that browser. 

Then, less than a year after I switched, they announced Dia and put Arc on life support. And now, it’s gone.  

I have limited interest in AI browsers, but even if I did, I would never switch to Dia? Why would I use a browser that could be sunset at any point? 

Chrome 4 life I guess. Fuck me for trying something new.

quotedTweet.text:
We've decided to sunset Arc on December 22, 2026.

That's not an easy sentence to write. We spent years building Arc and celebrating each and every release along the way: we have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community.

Our priority is to deliver best-in-class security for our members. Keeping a browser secure takes constant, dedicated work that is only increasing in the age of AI. Dia was built from the ground up to meet today’s security standards, so that's where our engineering and security teams will focus moving forward.

We've worked to make switching to @diabrowser as easy as possible for Arc members. Here's how:

· Your passwords, bookmarks, extensions and history come over to Dia seamlessly.
· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.
· Dia now surpasses Arc benchmarks in stability, speed, and security.
· The browser features you use in Arc are free in Dia, and the AI is optional.

Thank you for using Arc, for pushing us to make it better, and for building alongside us. The team that made Arc is the same team behind Dia, and some of our most ambitious work is just ahead. We'd love for you to be there with us when it lands.

卧槽！！才上线3个月的AI小工具，每月收5.4万美金了。

只做一件事，输入一个主题，一键生成一条YouTube纪录片。

就这么一个简单功能，再也简单不过，一句话就能讲清！

改产品已有1112个人付费了，算下来平均每人每月贡献大概$49。

这些在 TrustMRR 刷到的，收入数据接了Stripe验证，都是真金白银。

分享的目的，当没方向时，去翻翻这些正在收钱的小产品，比自己闷头想更有方向多了。

多看这些离钱近一点的东西。

我习惯这样看的，就 4 步👇

1、先按月增长排序，看看最近哪些产品涨得快，重点关注。

2、优先看上线不到半年的，如果产品还新，更容易看清它最初靠什么吸引用户。

3、把用月订阅收入除以付费订阅数，了解平均每个用户每月花多少钱。

4、往下翻，找收入验证信息。优先看接了 Stripe 验证的，数据更有参考价值。

像这个ai工具，你一句话就能听懂它卖什么，也能想明白谁会用它。

很简单，极简小而美。

出海方向，我想其实可以先从这样的产品看起的。

看看谁愿意付钱，又是在为什么付钱，也有判断价值。

出海野路子系列会持续更新~~~

如果对你有点启发，我感到很高兴！🍻

text:
有一次，孙哥携带我，和朋友们一起就餐。
在大家纷纷起身，觥筹交错，举杯畅饮之际。
他的敌蜜假装不经意地问：“孙哥，你多高。”
想要一举击溃孙哥。

没想到，孙哥居然面不改色地回答：“我1米75。”
我不可置信地看着他，那一瞬间，第一次体会到了来自爱人的背刺。

我以为爱情是两个人共同面对世界，没想到关键时刻，他竟然选择了独自长高。

“那你呢”客户问。
我看了看眼神坚毅的孙哥，为了爱情，我只好说，“我1米66。”

爱情的忠贞就在于此，
像险峰，增加你的高度，衬托你的威仪。
不仅爱你伟岸的身躯， 也爱你坚持的位置，足下的鞋垫。

这次美国的弹药不是很充足，所以打的话，个人觉得只能高火力轰炸两三天。

不过本次参与的国家非常多。如果你们最近真的有跟踪这条线的话，沙特跟也门已经在交火当中了，胡塞、伊朗、以色列等各方现在态度都很强硬。

我从今天开始会重启之前的"US Iran Daily"系列。

text:
评测分数涨了，Agent 实际却没变好。做 Eval 最怕的就是这种「假进步」，而且它往往不是 Prompt 的问题，是 Eval 本身的问题。

Anthropic 这篇工程博客讲的就是怎么避免它，还把整套流程做成了 Claude Code 的两个命令。

① /claude-api build-eval

自动构建评估集，优先从真实任务和失败案例中选题，还会检查评分器是否稳定。同一份输出判两次，如果结果不一致，就得先检查 Eval。

② /claude-api hillclimb

让 Claude 自动改进 Prompt、Skill 或 Harness，每轮提出一项修改，再用训练集和留出测试集验证。

如果训练集分数涨了，测试集却没提升，就撤回修改，避免 Agent 只记住几个失败案例。

而且当连续优化没有效果时，它还会反过来检查 Eval 本身有没有问题，比如题目含糊、评分规则写错。

实际案例中，他们在 44 个客服工单上做优化，最终把单次成本降到了约 1/5，留出集准确率从 78.6% 提升到 90.5%。不过样本量不大，还不能直接推广。

我觉得最值得抄的是两步：评分器判两次看是否一致，以及优化卡住时让 Agent 反过来质疑 Eval。评分器自己都不稳，后面分数的涨跌就没有意义。

但有一点要注意：每轮都用测试集决定是否保留修改，测试集其实也在参与调参。如果用它跑自动 hillclimb，我会额外留一份完全没碰过的数据，在那份数据上不涨，就说明是在给测试集调参，该回滚。

做 Agent Eval、或者正在手动调 Prompt 和 Skill 的，建议先收藏。

原文：https://t.co/rBxLiS1CjA

大家都知道，一旦拿了美国护照或者美国绿卡，美国国税局（IRS）就会像影子一样追着你搞“全球征税”，哪怕你逃到天涯海角赚钱也得给山姆大叔交最高 37% 的联邦个税和 20% 以上的资本利得税。

但全美国唯一留了一个合法的“免税飞地漏洞”，就是位于加勒比海的美国海外领地：波多黎各（Puerto Rico）！

不用放弃美国身份就能合法跟联邦税局说拜拜，难怪这几年把岛上的海景别墅全买爆了🥲

text:
Building native apps is something you can really handle if you have the 20x plan. If you're on the 1x or 5x plan, I think you should use ready-made libraries. Electron or Tauri can make sense there, because AI models use far fewer tokens with them, have low error rates, there are lots of packages, and most importantly you can ship cross-platform.

But if you say you want to put in the effort, you can look into Swift. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who doesn't have the 20x plan.

quotedTweet.text:
I just built a Mac app with Swift. Its speed, CPU usage and memory were amazing, but I got stuck with AI many times and kept giving it corrections, which drove me crazy.

There aren’t many ready-made libraries, and I think AI knows Swift less well. It codes incredibly fast and clean in Python, Rust and TypeScript, and ready-made libraries speed the work up even more, but the speed, memory and CPU side ends up being terrible.

Which one you pick is up to you, but GPUI also does cross-platform native, so take a look at it. Swift isn’t mandatory, you can build native apps with Rust too.

text:
Dots 当初就该单独做个 app！！！我越想越觉得 OpenAI 亏了！

兄弟们，Claude Duet 一出来，人家直接就是一个新 app，手机上点开就知道它是干嘛的：主动找你、你走开了接着干、动手前先问你。

再看 Dots，9 月底就上线了，比 Duet 早了快一个月，结果是塞在 ChatGPT 里面的。第一次还得跑到电脑上设置，设好了才能在手机 ChatGPT 里跟它聊。说白了，一个主动型 Agent，入口却藏在一个聊天 app 里，存在感一下就弱了。很多人可能到现在都不知道自己的 ChatGPT 里有这么个东西。

当然 OpenAI 也有它的算盘，几亿用户本来就在 ChatGPT 里，不用再劝你下一个新 app，Tibo 还说 Pro 里全包、聊天不扣周额度。一个押流量，一个押产品形态。

讲道理，你觉得 Agent 该单独做个 app，还是就该住在聊天框里？⬇️

text:
美国有家公司叫 Papa，居然把养老做成了滴滴模式，估值一度超过百亿元人民币！

它的商业模式非常有意思。

平台不建养老院，直接招募年轻人上门陪伴独居老人，帮忙买菜、做饭、打扫卫生、教用手机，甚至陪同就医。

年轻人按订单赚钱，老人按需预约，就跟滴滴打车一样。

更厉害的是它的盈利模式。

老年人孤独、缺乏照顾，可能带来更高的医疗支出。平台直接跟保险公司合作，由保险公司买单，让符合条件的老人免费享受陪伴服务。

保险公司希望减少医疗开支，年轻人获得工作机会，老人也有人照顾。

就靠这套模式，Papa 在2021年拿到1.5亿美元融资，估值达到14亿美元。

但我觉得最值得思考的是：

以前养老靠子女、靠养老院，现在连陪伴都能平台化、商业化了。

未来老龄化越来越严重，这种共享养老模式，会不会成为下一个大生意？

text:
Andrew Courtney raises a fair question: is the prediction-market boom delivering on its promise?

But the products that seem frivolous should not obscure the exchanges approaching this business as serious trading markets—developing contracts that help businesses and individuals price uncertainty and hedge real economic risk. That function has enduring value, whatever other products attract attention or volume.

Sports may also be an entry point. Someone who starts trading sports outcomes can learn about probabilities, pricing, liquidity, and managing a position. That experience may spark interest in other markets, including stock options. The products and risks differ, but the opportunity to broaden financial participation matters.

I would judge the industry by whether it builds useful markets, earns participants’ trust, and expands their ability to understand and manage risk. Some flaky contracts do not negate that potential.

text:
Harness is dead, long live the harness?

I went to @aiDotEngineer NYC and heard some very strong opinions about harnesses. Some engineers are removing parts of theirs because the models no longer need them. Others are building systems that let an agent work for days.

Of course, my immediate instinct was to sort things out and understand what is happening with harness (and if it’s really dead).

So many questions:
- What is an agent actually doing during those days?
- How does it remember what happened without turning an earlier guess into a fact?
- And if it can build its own tools, what are we letting it change?

This episode starts with a coding agent in about 25 lines of code, and then I drew insights from @_philschmid, @dillonrolnick, @aparnadhinak, @akshat_b, and a lot from @jediahkatz who had an amazing talk.

It came out as a full guide with everything you need to know about the current state of harness

Watch the full guide on YouTube: https://t.co/GWt9s6uZCs

text:
MIRACLES HAVE CEASED 

The writing below pales in comparison to what I’ve experienced. I’ve seen the lame walk, the sick healed, dead things brought back to life—and the captives set free. Starting with me. And all outside a ‘Church building.’ Just so we’re clear. 

You can debate theology all day long, but you cannot erase testimony. I can’t unsee what I’ve seen. 

————————————————-

It’s otherworldly to witness the relentless cycle of ‘anti-Christ theology’ preached by those who profess to ‘follow Christ.’ More specifically, the endless rhetoric that suggests apostleship, divine healing, and miraculous works have ceased—while the very works of God’s Kingdom continue to be witnessed across the Globe each and every day. Again, starting right here. 

“Then clean out the children’s cancer wards.”

Stop being so stiff-necked, cynical—and anti-Christ (Acts 7:51). It doesn’t work that way. Only a religious and bitter Bible belligerent—who claims to be a ‘Christ-follower’ would talk such foolishness. 

The Lord is sovereign. You cannot forsake the New Covenant and function in it at the same time. Meaning, you can’t deny signs, wonders, and miracles on a regular basis—but especially teach that—and be involved in them at the same time. 

Healing is not a formula we control, a power we command, or an outcome we can demand. And it certainly doesn’t happen just because certain sensationalists keep preaching “just stand on the finished work of Jesus.” 

Jesus Himself, did few miracles in His hometown—even though He very well could have. That should reveal something hidden. God doesn’t work in rebellion, and non stop disobedience and cynicism. He works through those who’ve surrendered  their lives to gain life (Matthew 10:39). 

The Great Commission doesn’t flow through the comfortable. It flows through the set-apart who believe. The consecrated, wholehearted saints who have denied themselves daily, taken up their cross, and followed Him into seasons of profound sacrifice, suffering, and lack. Every angle of Scripture points to this reality—and even then, the Spirit distributes His gifts as He determines (1 Corinthians 12:11).  There are still parts of the Kingdom that are a profound mystery apart from the simple things Christ taught us. 

But where, in the Western Church, will you find this type of Christian anymore? The kind who will surrender everything, endure the wilderness, embrace the cost, and obey Him (Acts 5:32)— regardless of what it costs them? Seriously. Where are they?

That may be one of the many—but perhaps primary—reasons these same Americanized Christians preach against the very words and works Christ, Himself, commissioned His followers to walk in. The uncomfortable truth? It is far easier to theologize away the supernatural than to surrender to the consecration, obedience, and cost of pursuing it. 

The Holy Spirit is not ours to command, but neither should we presume that a life of lukewarm compromise, worldly attachment, and deliberate cynicism is conducive to the manifestation of His power. Scripture is so clear about this. 

We can’t be obsessed with theology wars, non-stop bickering, politics, worldly living—idolatry, distraction, envy, jealousy, greed, competition, apologetics sessions and marketing our ‘Christian brands’ for engagement, clicks, and/or  followings—this ‘SELF-CARE, ACCUMULATION, and PROJECT ME type of ‘Christianity’—and expect the Spirit to move in us and through us on an increasing basis. That’s much too flimsy and weak of a foundation to steward such responsibility. Power in the wrong hands kills. Even if it’s meant for good. 

Perhaps it’s time for ‘professing Christian’s’ to stop preaching and creating theologies against the very works of the Spirit they claim to represent—and start examining whether their theology is faithfully reflecting the Christ they profess to follow (Romans 15:17-19). 

The further you go into His Kingdom, the less of the world you can take with you.

MIRACLES HAVE CEASED 

The writing below pales in comparison to what I’ve experienced. I’ve seen the lame walk, the sick healed, dead things brought back to life—and the captives set free. Starting with me. And all outside a ‘Church building.’ Just so we’re clear. 

You can debate theology all day long, but you cannot erase testimony. I can’t unsee what I’ve seen. 

————————————————-

It’s otherworldly to witness the relentless cycle of ‘anti-Christ theology’ preached by those who profess to ‘follow Christ.’ More specifically, the endless rhetoric that suggests apostleship, divine healing, and miraculous works have ceased—while the very works of God’s Kingdom continue to be witnessed across the Globe each and every day. Again, starting right here. 

“Then clean out the children’s cancer wards.”

Stop being so stiff-necked, cynical—and anti-Christ (Acts 7:51). It doesn’t work that way. Only a religious and bitter Bible belligerent—who claims to be a ‘Christ-follower’ would talk such foolishness. 

The Lord is sovereign. You cannot forsake the New Covenant and function in it at the same time. Meaning, you can’t deny signs, wonders, and miracles on a regular basis—but especially teach that—and be involved in them at the same time. 

Healing is not a formula we control, a power we command, or an outcome we can demand. And it certainly doesn’t happen just because certain sensationalists keep preaching “just stand on the finished work of Jesus.” 

Jesus Himself, did few miracles in His hometown—even though He very well could have. That should reveal something hidden. God doesn’t work in rebellion, and non stop disobedience and cynicism. He works through those who’ve surrendered  their lives to gain life (Matthew 10:39). 

The Great Commission doesn’t flow through the comfortable. It flows through the set-apart who believe. The consecrated, wholehearted saints who have denied themselves daily, taken up their cross, and followed Him into seasons of profound sacrifice, suffering, and lack. Every angle of Scripture points to this reality—and even then, the Spirit distributes His gifts as He determines (1 Corinthians 12:11).  There are still parts of the Kingdom that are a profound mystery apart from the simple things Christ taught us. 

But where, in the Western Church, will you find this type of Christian anymore? The kind who will surrender everything, endure the wilderness, embrace the cost, and obey Him (Acts 5:32)— regardless of what it costs them? Seriously. Where are they?

That may be one of the many—but perhaps primary—reasons these same Americanized Christians preach against the very words and works Christ, Himself, commissioned His followers to walk in. The uncomfortable truth? It is far easier to theologize away the supernatural than to surrender to the consecration, obedience, and cost of pursuing it. 

The Holy Spirit is not ours to command, but neither should we presume that a life of lukewarm compromise, worldly attachment, and deliberate cynicism is conducive to the manifestation of His power. Scripture is so clear about this. 

We can’t be obsessed with theology wars, non-stop bickering, politics, worldly living—idolatry, distraction, envy, jealousy, greed, competition, apologetics sessions and marketing our ‘Christian brands’ for engagement, clicks, and/or  followings—this ‘SELF-CARE, ACCUMULATION, and PROJECT ME type of ‘Christianity’—and expect the Spirit to move in us and through us on an increasing basis. That’s much too flimsy and weak of a foundation to steward such responsibility. Power in the wrong hands kills. Even if it’s meant for good. 

Perhaps it’s time for ‘professing Christian’s’ to stop preaching and creating theologies against the very works of the Spirit they claim to represent—and start examining whether their theology is faithfully reflecting the Christ they profess to follow (Romans 15:17-19). 

The further you go into His Kingdom, the less of the world you can take with you.

text:
Meta Ads CPMs are skyrocketing.

This is the most expensive CPMs on Meta have been during "normal" selling periods in the last ~18 months. 

We track billions in ad spend across thousands of advertisers. This is the trend we're seeing in our data.

On average across all our advertisers, CPMs are going up in 2026. 

There was a slight increase through Q1 2025, then CPMs plateaued for the rest of the year. 

Then at the start of 2026, CPMs began to rise. They peaked and stabilized all summer, but now are rising again. 

We are at +25% increase in CPMs compared to the same time last year. 

The Black Friday Cyber Monday CPM spike we saw in 2025 didn't start until November. 

This year we're seeing this spike happen in September. 

While CPMs aren't a core metric, they are a basic measure for how far your dollar goes on Meta. High CPMs can eat away at the efficiency in your account. 

But what is causing this increase?

Our data cannot identify a root cause, we can only demonstrate that something is happening. 

Meta made a ton of changes in the last year. The algorithm is just different now. 

For example, Meta rolled out changes to click through attribution in March 2026 - and CPMs rose to new normals immediately following. 

It's correlation, not causation. So what are advertisers supposed to do?

This much is clear:

What qualifies as "normal" performance on Meta is changing

Advertisers must adjust their expectations, arithmetic, and strategies to this new normal. 

The future is here and now. It will destroy advertisers who cannot adapt.

Charts and analysis by @bryanbumgardner 🛰️

I wanted to share a little about Gist, and why we’re building it.

When I first started thinking about the project, one direction I considered was an AI companion or assistant. There are real needs those products can serve. The question I kept coming back to was how to build something durable when so much of its capability depends on an underlying model you don’t own. I didn’t have a convincing answer for what we would build.

At the same time, I was becoming more interested in what AI might make possible for a small team building a social platform.

Social media is an established business, but starting something new has historically required substantial resources across engineering, product, content, and marketing. By late 2025, it seemed increasingly possible that AI could lower some of those barriers.

Many of the technical problems have known solutions. Putting them together well is still a lot of work. But I thought it was worth exploring whether a small team could now do that work with much more limited resources.

That would only get us part of the way. A product can work well and still give people little reason to use it. Building a community, earning trust, and creating something people want to return to are questions we have to answer through the experience itself.

There is a natural connection with AppLovin’s business and technology. That helped make the idea worth pursuing. But what has made it more meaningful to me is the people we’ve met along the way.

At a recent dinner with Gist creators, I heard people talk about why they share what they know. They wanted to be useful, help someone through a problem, or bring a perspective that might make another person’s life a little better. I left thinking about how much that sense of purpose matters.

That is the kind of place we hope Gist can become. Somewhere people find ideas worth their time, and where creators can build something meaningful and sustainable around what they have to offer.

We can build the technology, but the people who bring their ideas and communities will give Gist its character. We have to keep listening and let what we learn shape the product.

Gist is now available on iOS and Android, with a 4.7 rating on the US App Store. We’re still early in user acquisition and aren’t pushing aggressively to grow. We’re using this period to understand what people value and where we need to do better.

Some of the most encouraging feedback has come from people who say Gist has given them a renewed sense of purpose in creating, or helped them feel better about their lives. It’s early, and we shouldn’t read too much into it. But it is meaningful to hear, and it gives us a reason to keep working.

If you give Gist a try, I’d be interested to hear what you think.

I wanted to share a little about Gist, and why we’re building it.

When I first started thinking about the project, one direction I considered was an AI companion or assistant. There are real needs those products can serve. The question I kept coming back to was how to build something durable when so much of its capability depends on an underlying model you don’t own. I didn’t have a convincing answer for what we would build.

At the same time, I was becoming more interested in what AI might make possible for a small team building a social platform.

Social media is an established business, but starting something new has historically required substantial resources across engineering, product, content, and marketing. By late 2025, it seemed increasingly possible that AI could lower some of those barriers.

Many of the technical problems have known solutions. Putting them together well is still a lot of work. But I thought it was worth exploring whether a small team could now do that work with much more limited resources.

That would only get us part of the way. A product can work well and still give people little reason to use it. Building a community, earning trust, and creating something people want to return to are questions we have to answer through the experience itself.

text:
Alright everyone (my four followers) it's been awhile since my first post. Just been working hard building an app with AI most of this year. It's finally in a good place that I wanted to post about it and gather any feeback on areas for improvement or missing features. 

The app is called Looped In. It's an AI native app with an AI assistant called Cue. The app is for every part of your life and each area gets its own Loop. The main feature is smart capture. Take a picture of flyer or schedule or paste a long email or text and it pulls out the dates, times, and tasks and puts them in a Loop. The idea came from my wife who was always struggling with our kids school, sports, and dance schedules, plus our work and church commitments and other things that compete for time and then all the apps she would have to jump between and try to keep things straight.

It's great to keep everything in one place and not having to jump between multiple apps all the time and provides a place to collaborate with others like friends, school or work groups, religious or community events, etc. You can have personal loops and shared loops. People that you share and collaborate loops with can only see those shared loops and not your personal loops. You can share details of events with friends or family members that don't have app so they can see the date, time and a google map link of the location.

I have a few other features that I haven't enabled yet to make it less overwhelming. There will be tabs for sign up sheets, carpool scheduler, group chats, storing files and links and a watchlist with price trends and updates.

It's on the App Store now. The first week is free, then creating Loops and saving smart captures needs Plus. Happy to give more time if you like it and are using it. People you invite join free for that loop they are invited to.  https://t.co/vrONlK2k7D

I'm happy to discuss the process I went through building it. I've had zero coding experience and spent all my career in accounting so it has been fun learning how to use AI as I go and create something from scratch that actually works. I've put extensive time and effort into the backend systems and architecture and security to make this app run and function like it was professionally built by a team of engineers. Please let me know what you think. I would really love any feedback good or bad. If you like it and think it's cool I would appreciate sharing the post and helping me spread the word.

text: Soon, smartcontracts on quantum-safe blockchains will feel much safer than banks. With AI-powered hackers, the perceived safety net of “it’s privately deployed, so it’s secure” is quickly disappearing.

quotedTweet.text:
MAJOR U.S. BANKS DETECT UNAUTHORIZED AI AGENTS ACCESSING CUSTOMER ACCOUNTS — AXIOS

Major banks, including $JPM, $BAC, $MS and $WFC, are confronting security risks from third-party AI agents accessing customer accounts, according to Axios.

Some agents have reportedly attempted actions beyond user instructions, raising concerns about unauthorized transactions and fund transfers.

Morgan Stanley has begun blocking third-party agents, while JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are restricting access.

Banks warn they cannot reliably distinguish legitimate user activity from autonomous AI agents, even when customers have voluntarily shared their credentials.
